About three minutes to order. Most filings are submitted to the state within one business day. Approval usually comes back in about a week.

No. Forming an LLC is a filing, not an application. Nobody runs your credit to register a company with a state.

I can't answer that for you, and I won't pretend to. What I can tell you is that plenty of founders form a standard LLC without one, and that's the practical path we handle. subject: You can't sign a lease as a vibe
body:
An LLC is not a certificate you frame. It's a set of doors that were locked, and now aren't.

Here's what's behind them.

A business bank account. A real one, in the company's name, not the same account your groceries come out of. Banks ask for your formation documents and your EIN, and you get both here. And once you have it, you keep business money and personal money strictly separate. For your books, for your sanity, and because that separation is the whole point of doing this properly.

Stripe and payment processing. Direct bookings, deposits, guest payments. All of it runs through the business instead of your personal account like this is a hobby.

Landlords and suppliers who take you seriously. You already know the difference between "hi, it's just me, I'm interested in your unit" and a formed company with an operating agreement and a registered agent on file. One of those emails gets answered.

Your home address off public records. Forming an LLC puts information onto a public government record. Do it yourself in a hurry and the address sitting on there is usually your apartment. We keep yours off it. That is not a small thing.

And fewer rookie mistakes. The kind that delay or void a brand new LLC and send you back to the start.

Then there's the long game, and I'll say this one carefully.

The LLC is what makes you fundable later. Not today. I'm not promising you a dollar of anything, and nobody honest would. But every serious conversation about business capital starts with "are you an actual business," and right now your answer is no. It doesn't have to be by next week.

That's what your state filing fee buys you. Not a certificate. A door.

https://buildmyllc.com/

What still gets me is how many people never walk through it because somebody quoted them a few hundred dollars and they closed the tab.

You already decided you wanted this business. You decided that months ago.

This is just the paperwork catching up to a decision you already made.

Inayah

An approved LLC gets you ready for a business bank account, Stripe, landlords treating you like a company, and your home address off public record. It is also what makes you fundable later. $0 from us: https://buildmyllc.com/ Our own company.

subject: What $0 doesn't get you
body:
Everybody selling you something reads you the list of what's included. Let me read you the other one.

Here's what an LLC does NOT do, and what our $0 does NOT cover. Read it before you order, not after.

It doesn't make you money. It's a legal wrapper. It won't find the unit, negotiate the lease or take the photos. That part is still you.

Your state still charges you. Our service fee is $0. Your state's filing fee is real, it's passed through at cost, and you see it before you confirm. Nobody can waive that.

Some states charge annual franchise taxes or fees, anywhere from $0 to $800 a year depending on where you form. That's the state, every year, no matter who filed for you.

Year two is not free. Your registered agent renews at a market-fair rate you'll see clearly before you ever pay it. No ambush. And most states want an annual report with its own fee, $0 to $500.

You have to keep your money strictly separate. Business account for business, personal for personal. Not "mostly." If guest income is landing in your personal checking and groceries are coming out of the business account, you are not really running a separate business - and that habit is on you, not on us or on the paperwork.

Self-employment tax still applies unless you later elect S-Corp status. That's a real conversation for down the road, with a real tax professional.

We don't provide legal or tax advice. We show you the practical steps other founders take. If you need an attorney or a CPA, hire one. That's the honest limit of what we do.

And the guarantee, stated plainly. If we make a filing error that causes your state to reject it, we fix it at our cost. State fees are non-refundable. Once the state has that money it's gone, and that's true no matter who files for you.

That's the full picture, before you spend a dime.

Now here's the thing.

Every one of those is true whether you file with us, hand a big name a few hundred dollars, or do it yourself at your kitchen table.

The only variable is whether you pay a service fee on top.

With us, you don't.

https://buildmyllc.com/

You've got everything now. There's nothing left to research.
